newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Metals - Zinc demand up, others seen quiet.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Metals - Zinc demand up, others seen quiet.

text.p: Recent declines in London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices has spurred zinc buying interest in the South Korean market, but other metals were quiet in lacklustre trading, traders said on Thursday.
"Early this week, there were some zinc volumes changing hands at 1.24 to 1.25 million won a tonne," a trader with Tong Yang Global said.
Domestic zinc prices fell to 1.245 million won a tonne this week on losses on the LME from 1.277 million won a week ago, while lead prices were unchanged at 744,000 won a tonne.

Another trader said a recent fall in U.S. aluminium premiums was expected to boost domestic demand but this would be limited due to Korea's economic downturn, the collapse of Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel, a weak local currency and January's labour unrest.

Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery were seen flat in a range of $85-$90 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME cash prices, but were expected to be lower next week on softening U.S. premiums, traders said.

Domestic aluminium prices fell to 1.52 million won a tonne this week, in line with lower levels on the London market, from 1.53 million won last week, while copper prices were seen flat at 2.345 million won a tonne.
South Korea's total aluminium rolling products sales rose 20 percent to 21,963 tonnes in March from 18,282 tonnes the previous month, traders said.
They said the sales included exports of 5,332 tonnes in March, compared with 4,637 tonnes in February.
